ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: $\triangle FGH$ is an equilateral triangle. Find $HG$.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle FGH, vertex F is above, H is at the lower left, and G is at the lower right. The left side FH is labeled as 6x + 1, the right side FG is labeled as 3x + 10, and the base HG is labeled as 9x - 8. Reasoning: The problem states that triangle FGH is an equilateral triangle, so the three sides are equal. Let FH = FG, then 6x + 1 = 3x + 10 can be obtained. Solving gives 3x = 9, therefore x = 3. HG is required, and in the figure HG = 9x - 8; substituting x = 3 gives HG = 9(3) - 8 = 27 - 8 = 19.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: triangle FGH has side HF labeled 6x+1, side FG labeled 3x+10, and base HG labeled 9x-8. From the text, triangle FGH is equilateral, so all three side lengths are equal. Set two side expressions equal, for example 6x+1 = 3x+10, solve to get x = 3, then substitute into the requested side HG = 9x-8 to get 9(3)-8 = 19.
